highlights.text: Write a little every day, even when it feels like nothing is happening.
Keep a file of sentences you wish you had written, and read it before you start.
highlights.note: Start this file tonight. Seed it with the opening of my favorite essay.

highlights.text: Edit on paper; it shows you what the screen hides.
During deep sleep, the brain replays the day's experiences and decides what to keep.
highlights.question: Which stage of sleep does the replaying, and how was it measured?
highlights.note: Ties in with the chapter on spaced repetition.

highlights.text: Memory is less a recording than a reconstruction, rebuilt a little differently each time we read it back.
highlights.note: Good quote for the talk on note-taking.

highlights.text: Short naps help, but only when they stay under thirty minutes.
highlights.question: Why does a longer nap stop helping?
highlights.answer: Past about 30 minutes you drop into deep sleep, and waking from it leaves you groggy (sleep inertia).

highlights.text: Body text needs a contrast ratio of at least 4.5 to 1 to stay readable.
highlights.question: How is the contrast ratio calculated?

highlights.text: Never rely on color alone to carry meaning.
highlights.note: Check the status badges on our dashboard: red and green only.

highlights.text: Lines of 50 to 75 characters are the easiest to read.
highlights.question: Where does the 50 to 75 range come from?
highlights.answer: Typography research on reading speed: long lines make the eye lose its place, short ones break the rhythm.

title: Keyboard shortcuts that save an hour a week

highlights.text: Learn one new shortcut each week and use it until it is automatic.
Most time is lost switching between the mouse and the keyboard.
Toast the spices in oil before the lentils go in.
highlights.question: Why toast spices in oil first?
highlights.answer: Many flavor compounds dissolve in fat, not water, so blooming them in oil spreads their taste through the dish.

highlights.text: A squeeze of lemon at the end brightens everything.

title: How to read a research paper in three passes

highlights.text: Read the abstract, the headings and the conclusion before anything else.
On the second pass, read the figures as carefully as the text.
highlights.note: Try this on the paper for Friday's reading group.
